title: The Well That Drank Water

full_text:
An honest vegetable farmer named Chennappa purchased a plot of land with an ancient stone well from a cunning landholder named Raghava. The sale deed clearly stated that the land and the well were transferred unconditionally.

However, two days after the sale, when Chennappa brought bullocks to pump water for his thirsty cabbage crops, the well was completely dry!
When Chennappa complained, Raghava laughed slyly:
'My good man, I sold you the well, but I never promised the water would stay! This well is an enchanted "Thirsty Well"; it drinks all water that enters it! If you want water, you must pay me a monthly fee of twenty silver coins to channel water from my neighboring tank!'

Chennappa, ruined by the sudden loss of water, appealed to Tenali Raman.
Tenali inspected the well. He dropped a heavy stone into the depths: it hit stone with a hollow, echoing thud.
Tenali took a small boat and rowed along the nearby canal belonging to Raghava’s estate, which ran twenty yards below the level of the well.
He noticed that the water in Raghava’s canal was unusually fresh, clear, and bubbling from a submerged stone archway.

Tenali returned to the dry well carrying five large bags of red powdered ochre dye.
In the presence of the village council, Tenali poured the red dye into the bottom of the dry well, followed by ten large barrels of water.
The water disappeared quickly down a fissure.

Tenali then led the council to Raghava’s canal:
Within twenty minutes, bright crimson-red water came gushing out of the submerged stone conduit into Raghava’s private canal!

Tenali pointed to the red water:
'Behold the "Thirsty Well"! Raghava had secretly chiseled an underground drainage pipe from the bottom of Chennappa’s well into his own lower canal! Whenever water accumulated in the well, it drained straight into Raghava’s private reservoir, stealing Chennappa’s water while Raghava demanded extortionate monthly fees!'

The village council was outraged by the deceit.
Raghava was ordered to seal the illegal drainage pipe with solid granite masonry, pay Chennappa fifty silver coins in restitution, and provide free irrigation for two seasons.
Chennappa’s well filled to the brim with sweet, abundant water, proving that deceitful schemes cannot hide from thorough investigation.
moral: Greedy landlords who construct deceitful deceptions to void legal sales are defeated by scientific investigation.

Acting in hasty anger without listening
